title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government’s reply to the 2020 committee report outlines plans to establish clear public standards for artificial intelligence, focusing on safety, reliability, and fairness. It stresses stronger regulation, ethical guidance, and oversight to ensure AI technologies serve the public good while protecting privacy and civil rights.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual explains how it will oversee the use of artificial intelligence in exams and qualifications, setting guidelines to keep assessments fair, reliable, and transparent. The policy aims to protect students and maintain public trust by ensuring AI tools are used responsibly and do not compromise the integrity of the qualifications system.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This document examines how copyright laws affect the training and use of AI systems, analyzing both the legal implications and potential economic impacts. It offers recommendations for balancing creators' rights with AI innovation while ensuring compliance with existing copyright frameworks.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has responded to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence, acknowledging the findings of the “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency” report. It outlines plans to foster responsible AI development, strengthen regulation, and invest in infrastructure and skills so that AI benefits society.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document sets out the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of a committee tasked with reviewing how artificial intelligence relates to public standards. It also provides frequently asked questions to help clarify the committee’s role and the review process.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the governance of artificial intelligence. In its submission, the organization highlights key concerns and offers recommendations for strengthening AI policy oversight.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy examines how artificial intelligence will change the way medical products are regulated. It focuses on applying the principles outlined in the AI White Paper to ensure safety, effectiveness, and transparency in healthcare technologies.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy explains how the organization will use AI to strengthen its military capabilities and keep pace with evolving security challenges. Its goal is to become the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential defence organization in the world relative to its size.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to harness the benefits of AI. It also sets guidelines for identifying, mitigating, and managing potential risks associated with AI implementation in transportation.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report reviews how copyright‑protected works are used to train and develop AI systems under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It outlines current practices, identifies challenges and legal gaps, and offers recommendations for ensuring that AI developers comply with copyright rules.
